back: An increase by the same percentage every period, so the quantity is multiplied by the same number (greater than 1) each time.
A decrease by the same percentage every period: the quantity is multiplied by the same number between 0 and 1 each time.
A fall in the value of an item over time, for example a car losing 15% of its value each year.

front: Value after $n$ periods of growth or decay at $r\%$
back: $V = P\left(1 \pm \dfrac{r}{100}\right)^n$ (plus for growth, minus for decay).

front: What is the yearly multiplier for depreciation of 12%?
Is losing 15% a year for 3 years the same as losing 45%?
back: No: the value is $0.85^3 = 0.614$ of the original, a loss of about 38.6%.

front: How do you find when a depreciating value first falls below half (no logarithms)?
back: Try powers of the multiplier: $0.85^4 = 0.522$, $0.85^5 = 0.444$, so 5 years. Show the values either side of the target.

front: After 2 years of 20% depreciation a laptop is worth US\$512. How do you find the original price?
What is the difference between straight-line and exponential depreciation?
back: Straight-line takes off the same **amount** each year; exponential takes off the same **percentage** of the current value.

front: Does an item losing 20% of its value each year ever become worth nothing?
back: No: it keeps 80% each year, so after 5 years it still has $0.8^5 \approx 32.8\%$ of its value.
